title: hello-prochat — a pro-grade multi-modal chat assistant (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “Web search, page fetch, image reading, image generation, a sandboxed code interpreter.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beats.

beats.label: Pre-flight the code interpreter
beats.cue: Python, JavaScript and Shell each run in a container — this probes all three images. A ✗ here means start Docker (or Podman) before you roll, not mid-take.

verify.note: probes python:3.13-slim / node:22-alpine / alpine:3.19 through the configured backend (CREWHAUS_SANDBOX, default docker). Exit 0 either way — a missing backend shows as ✗ with the reason, which is the point of the beat: the run-math beat needs these green

beats.label: Pick the image-generation fallback
beats.cue: OPENAI_API_KEY wins whenever it's set. This line is what makes /imagine degrade to a placeholder instead of a hard error when it isn't.

verify.note: tool-image-generation resolves OPENAI_API_KEY → openai, else CREWHAUS_IMAGE_PROVIDER=mock → mock, else openai (which then throws “OPENAI_API_KEY is not set”). Without this export there is no fallback

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec, block by block

beats.label: The header: what it is, what to ask it
beats.cue: A tier-one chat app in a terminal — and the four prompts that prove it.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: Two lines: what it's called, and which runtime spine to compile.

beats.label: The model, and what it can reach
beats.cue: Sonnet, then the manifest: search, fetch, see, generate, ingest, execute, delegate.

beats.label: The Method
beats.cue: Search first for anything recent, Python for anything numeric — and no tool theater.

beats.label: Style
beats.cue: “Match the user's register.” And be willing to say “I don't know” before guessing.

beats.label: The rules that fence it in
beats.cue: The sandbox can't reach your host — so it never promises to save anything to ~/Downloads.

beats.label: One sub-agent: web-researcher
beats.cue: 3-5 searches, 2-3 fetches, back with a cited brief under 250 words — in its own context.

beats.label: Nine tools
beats.cue: Notice what's absent: no read, no write, no edit, no bash on your machine.

beats.label: Web, vision, images, ingest
beats.cue: All always-on — this is a research-and-chat agent, and none of it touches your filesystem.

beats.label: Code execution, always-on
beats.cue: Python, JavaScript and Shell need no prompt because each call runs in a throwaway container — network=none, read-only root, image allowlist. Your host filesystem is not reachable from them.

beats.label: And the sub-agent dispatch grant
beats.cue: One more rule, easy to miss: Task. That's the grant the /browse beat spends two groups from now — no Task rule, no sub-agent fan-out.

beats.label: Compact on a cheap model
beats.cue: Older turns get summarized on Haiku, so a long conversation stays cheap.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the scope audit — nothing emitted yet.

beats.label: Audit its own tool grants
beats.cue: The keyword ranker wants to hand it read, write, edit and bash. This spec withholds them.

verify.note: keyword-ranks builtins against agent.instructions; the host-side tools it proposes are deliberately not granted

beats.label: Emit the lowered IR
beats.cue: The spec is sugar. Lower it to JSON — too long for a terminal, so send it to a file.

verify.note: writes the lowered IR (~96 lines) instead of paging it; the inlined instructions string is the long part

beats.label: Open the IR
beats.cue: Nine tools, ten permission rules, one sub-agent, the compaction model — what the compiler actually sees, and nothing invented.

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: --check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN with no key.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: Nine tools, one sub-agent, every permission rule — one TypeScript program you own.

beats.label: Launch the chat REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] crewhaus run compiles in memory and drops into a streaming chat loop.

verify.note: interactive REPL; needs Anthropic credentials. The boot banner is five lines before “agent ready”: continuity on · 4 skills · 12 slash commands (the starter's six plus continuity's six) · 1 sub-agent · “[sandbox] assuming docker”

beats.label: Just talk to it
beats.cue: [needs-key] Plain chat — no tools fire. The model just answers.
beats.text: what's the capital of Burkina Faso?

beats.label: Make it do arithmetic
beats.cue: [needs-key] It reaches for Python on its own — /code is optional. Watching it decide is the demo.

verify.note: the Python tool shells out to `docker run python:3.13-slim` — needs the backend the setup-sandbox beat probed, and the image already pulled, or the first call blocks on a multi-hundred-MB pull mid-take

beats.label: Summarize a URL
beats.cue: [needs-key] Fetches the page and returns a three-sentence summary.

beats.label: Fan out the researcher
beats.cue: [needs-key] web-researcher returns a TL;DR, five cited facts, open questions, and sources.
beats.text: /browse latest news on the Anthropic Claude 4.7 release

verify.note: WebSearch needs CREWHAUS_SEARCH_PROVIDER + CREWHAUS_SEARCH_API_KEY as well as the model key

beats.label: Generate an image
beats.cue: [needs-key] DALL-E when OPENAI_API_KEY is set; otherwise the mock placeholder, surfaced verbatim — because Setup exported the fallback.
beats.text: /imagine a lobster wearing a top hat, oil-painting style

verify.note: ImageGenerate resolves openai when OPENAI_API_KEY is set. The placeholder is NOT a built-in default: it comes from the setup-image-provider beat's CREWHAUS_IMAGE_PROVIDER=mock — without that export the tool throws “OPENAI_API_KEY is not set — required for provider=openai”

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell.

groups.title: One more thing · the same agent, somewhere else

beats.label: A skill the model loads itself
beats.cue: Markdown with triggers — it self-loads when a question smells like research. No recompile.

beats.label: A slash command is a Markdown file
beats.cue: Six ship in .crewhaus/commands/ — /imagine is just a prompt the model follows literally.

beats.label: Export it as a Claude Code plugin
beats.cue: The same spec, emitted as a plugin dir — four files: the manifest, a README, the researcher as a Claude Code sub-agent, and the persona itself as a skill. The authored skills and the six slash commands stay behind: this projects the spec, not the .crewhaus/ tree.

verify.note: “exported hello-prochat (cli) … 4 files, smoke check ✓” — .claude-plugin/plugin.json, README.md, agents/web-researcher.md, skills/hello-prochat/SKILL.md (that skill is agent.instructions, not the authored research-topic one)

beats.label: Or serve it as an MCP tool
beats.cue: [needs-key] serve --mcp projects the whole agent as one MCP tool — `chat` — that your IDE can call. It prints two lines and then blocks: the terminal belongs to the server until you Ctrl-C it.

verify.note: long-running stdio MCP server: prints the continuity line + “[serve] MCP stdio server for "hello-prochat" ready (tools: chat)”, then blocks until SIGINT (“[serve] stopped.”). Every tool call runs the agent, so it needs provider credentials — and the drive closes on the editor beat below, not on this terminal

beats.label: Close on the exported researcher
beats.cue: Your sub-agent, now a Claude Code sub-agent. One spec, more than one runtime.
